On WebVoyager-Static, the 4B Mage-VL-Cowork SFT model achieves 58.6% success (377/643 tasks; Table 4), ranking second overall behind the specialized browser agent Fara1.5-4B (68.0%).
Comparing previously published live WebVoyager scores against our offline evaluation reveals a drop of 12.8 to 33.1 percentage points across the five models with self-reported live results

because the standard live judge inspects only the final screenshot and explicitly instructs the evaluator to trust unsupported claims in the agent’s text (“choose to believe the content”), it rewards fluent guessing and masks three recurring failure modes in current web agents

uncommitted stateful interactions, where agents fill out forms or click preliminary buttons and declare success while the backend database records no actual mutation (e.g., an empty cart or unsubmitted booking)

shortcut answering from search snippets or parametric memory, where agents answer after a few steps from a result card or prior knowledge without opening the detail page that holds the ground-truth evidence

By jointly verifying page-visit traces, ground-truth constraints, and backend database state, WebVoyager-Static removes these false positives and provides a more diagnostic reference for evaluating genuine multi-step web interaction.
Each replica runs as a local Flask and SQLite service with target domains routed to the local host.

Before every episode, the environment restores a fresh working database from a read-only seed snapshot, isolating stateful operations across rollouts while exposing the underlying tables for deterministic verification.

we capture reference snapshots from target websites—spanning DOM hierarchies, computed CSS rules, and static assets (logos, icons, and inline SVGs), supplemented by web archives when live endpoints are restricted—and reconstruct the full page structure.

Beyond static layout, we implement the interactive controls required for end-to-end task completion, including multi-attribute filter panels, date pickers, sorting menus, pagination, stateful submission forms, and domain-specific components such as Leaflet maps and Chart.js views.

We populate each replica’s seed database primarily from authentic structured sources, including public APIs and data dumps (e.g., ESPN, Stack Exchange, Hacker News, and OpenStreetMap), web crawl archives, and bibliographic catalogs.

Moreover, we establish a new benchmark by compiling real-world tasks from 15 popular websites and introduce an automatic evaluation protocol leveraging multimodal understanding abilities of GPT-4V to evaluate open-ended web agents.
We show that WebVoyager achieves a 59.1% task success rate on our benchmark, significantly surpassing the performance of both GPT-4 (All Tools) and the WebVoyager (text-only) setups
The proposed automatic evaluation metric achieves 85.3% agreement with human judgment, indicating its effectiveness in providing reliable and accurate assessments of web agents.

We select 15 representative websites that cover different aspects of our daily life to ensure diversity in our evaluation, including Allrecipes, Amazon, Apple, ArXiv, BBC News, Booking, Cambridge Dictionary, Coursera, ESPN, GitHub, Google Flights, Google Map, Google Search, Huggingface, and Wolfram Alpha.
